newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea plans to charge 56 leftist students.
newsitem.headline: South Korea plans to charge 56 leftist students.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Friday summoned 56 leaders of a banned pro-North Korean student group, saying they would be charged for violating the country's National Security law.
"We are determined to charge them with violating the National Security Law for their activities benefiting the enemy," one prosecution official told Reuters.
The law, which calls for the maximum penalty of death by hanging, prohibits all activities praising or benefiting North Korea.
But prosecution officials also said leniency would be granted to students who denounced the leftist Hanchongryon group and turned themselves in.

One prosecution official said 499 students remained active members of the Hanchongryon, of which 42 had been arrested for violating the security law. The remainder would be summoned within the next two months.
The government in June banned the Hanchongryon, which has organised a number of violent street protests earlier this year, saying it had been taking orders from Stalinist Pyongyang.
The move followed an admission of responsibility by the group for the torture killing of a suspected police spy.

In June, police arrested three Hanchongryon activists over the fatal beating of Lee Suk, a factory worker. More than 200 Hanchonryon members have also been arrested in connection with violent protests.
Of 206 university councils affiliated with Hanchongryon, 134 have publicly quit the umbrella organisation since the government ban.
